A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QWEM research despite substantial retitling and revision. Their complete main texts, mathematical appendices, experimental descriptions, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original training experiments, analogy benchmark comparisons, subsampling analyses, and validation of an analogy-accuracy estimator in Figures 1–10 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 reports original word2vec/QWEM comparisons, three benchmark evaluations, feature-overlap measurements, and task-vector spectral analyses in Figures 1–6 and Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: V2 changes QWEM training from v1's unigram-based subsampling to separate word-pair weights, explicitly using Ψ+ = Ψ− = (Pij + PiPj)^−1 before the dynamic-window adjustment. This changes the objective's weighting and enables the constant-G formulation. The shared-embedding architecture remains, while Lxe is no longer an evaluated variant.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates downstream analogy completion using Google Analogies. V2 retains that task and adds human-rated semantic similarity evaluation on MEN and WordSim353, substantially broadening the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds word2vec to the training-dynamics comparisons and word2vec/PPMI to the feature comparisons. Its benchmark comparison drops Lxe while retaining the target-SVD, PMI, and PPMI methods. V1's gensim SGNS comparator is replaced by the authors' GPU implementation under v2's shared-embedding setup.

E3.justification: The Wikipedia training subset changes from 200,000 articles and 135 million words to 1.58 million articles and 2 billion tokens, with new article-length filtering. Numerals are discarded instead of spelled out. V2 adds standard-initialization comparisons, specifies a 90% learning-rate drop for benchmark runs instead of v1's occasional linear annealing, and introduces Spearman correlation for the similarity benchmarks.

E4.justification: V1's subsampling sweep, early-accuracy-peak analysis, superposition example, critical-size estimator validation, and smooth-metric analysis are removed. V2 adds comparisons across initialization scales, quantitative feature-overlap heatmaps, task-vector localization and spectral analyses, and signal-to-noise comparisons across semantic categories. Appendix A also reports normalization checks.

E5.justification: Statistical estimation changes from v1's moment-matched Gaussian surrogate for analogy accuracy to v2's Marchenko-Pastur fitting procedure, which estimates noise scale from centered task-vector variance and manually fits the aspect ratio (Appendix A.6). Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V1 Figure 2D reports 63.57% for Lsym and 71.66% for SGNS; v2 Figure 3 reports 65.1% for QWEM and 68.0% for word2vec. These are replaced results under changed training conditions, not comparable performance gains or losses. V2 additionally reports MEN/WordSim353 scores, feature overlaps, and spiked-spectrum findings, while removing v1's critical-size prediction results.

T1.justification: The main results are reformulated around constant or rank-one pair-weight matrices instead of v1's Lxe subsampling assumptions. Result 3 states embedding convergence modulo rotations using rescaled time. Appendix C replaces v1 Appendix D.2's incorrect identification of triangular diagonal entries with singular values by an asymptotic perturbation argument. The analogy-accuracy estimator is removed, and task-vector spectral definitions are introduced.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes solving a broad QWEM class and predicting when analogy completion begins at a critical model size. V2 centers its contributions on a faithful word2vec proxy, including agreement in dynamics and learned features, and replaces the critical-size prediction contribution with a random-matrix account of linear semantic representations.

C2.justification: V2 interprets task-vector quality through informative versus noisy eigen-features, explaining how additional dimensions can eventually reduce signal-to-noise ratio. This replaces v1's emphasis on analogy-onset thresholds and early accuracy peaks. V2 also explicitly acknowledges the unfinished rigorous justification of Result 3, limited experimental scale, and absence of GloVe comparisons.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public-code link, GPU implementation and streaming details, hardware specifications, corpus-filtering instructions, and spectral-fitting procedures. It omits v1 Appendix C.3's experiment-by-experiment learning rates and step counts. Its new timing disclosures conflict: Section 3.3 gives 75 minutes for Figure 3 training, whereas Appendix A.5 gives 12 hours.

R1.justification: V2 adds task-arithmetic and random-matrix references, including Ilharco et al. and Baik et al., and expands comparisons with matrix-factorization and contrastive-learning theory. It removes much of the LLM-emergence and analogy-explanation literature. Research positioning shifts toward a faithful, analytically tractable account of word2vec feature learning.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and extensively rewritten around word2vec and linear representations. Related work is integrated into the introduction, the analogy-reasoning section is replaced, and the conclusion becomes a discussion. Appendices are reorganized from relationships/proofs/experiments/derivations into experiments/additional figures/proofs/relationships.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. The overview and dynamics figures are substantially redesigned around paired word2vec/QWEM displays. V1's benchmark bar chart is replaced by feature and benchmark tables in v2 Figure 3, and new spectral panels and overlap heatmaps replace several earlier appendix plots.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central proxy-model justification through direct word2vec/QWEM comparisons of dynamics and features, alongside broader benchmark validation. It also removes a concrete mathematical error in v1's QR argument and states the remaining rigor limitations more clearly. These gains improve the paper's scientific support and precision enough to outweigh the narrower scope after removing the critical-size estimator. Missing explicit training settings and conflicting runtime disclosures remain reproducibility weaknesses.
